description: Example template for uops.info instruction cost data

_mm256_permutexvar_epi32.note: VPERMD ymm, ymm, ymm - Variable permute across lanes

_mm256_permute4x64_epi64.note: VPERMQ ymm, ymm, imm8 - Permute 64-bit elements

_mm256_permute_ps.note: VPERMILPS ymm, ymm, imm8 - Permute within 128-bit lanes

_mm256_shuffle_ps.note: VSHUFPS ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8 - Two-input shuffle

_mm256_unpacklo_epi32.note: VPUNPCKLDQ ymm, ymm, ymm - Interleave low 32-bit

_mm256_unpackhi_epi32.note: VPUNPCKHDQ ymm, ymm, ymm - Interleave high 32-bit

_mm256_permute2x128_si256.note: VPERM2I128 ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8 - Cross-lane permute

_mm256_blend_ps.note: VBLENDPS ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8 - Immediate blend

_mm256_blendv_ps.note: VBLENDVPS ymm, ymm, ymm, ymm - Variable blend

_mm256_alignr_epi32.note: VALIGND ymm, ymm, ymm, imm8 - Concatenate and shift

instructions_note: To populate with real data, visit https://uops.info/ and look up each instruction for your target CPU
how_to_use: 1. Copy this file to uops_data_{cpu_model}.json (e.g., uops_data_zen5.json)
2. Visit https://uops.info/ for your target CPU
3. Look up each instruction and fill in actual latency/throughput/ports
4. The system will automatically load the data when you use CostModel(cpu_model)
